appendix.fallback_scale_note: These test years have no earlier year to fit the utility scale on and fall back to the predeclared theoretical value. The utility is divided by the scale, so the fallback amplifies corrections where a fitted scale halves them: their stakes and claimed edges are several times any fitted year's and are not comparable with them. Exclude these years from any return figure -- filter on is_honest_scale in the per-run CSV.

sensitivity.note: fitted on strictly earlier years; fallback to the theoretical value

appendix.unverifiable_gates: An interaction diagnostic across predeclared cohorts, reproduction from a clean identified commit, and confirmation on a future prospective period are not derivable from these artifacts. Production remains the five-seed Offset ensemble until they are met.

utility_scale.theory_source: the scale the fallback year used, which is the predeclared theoretical value

effects.reason: There are no per-feature effects to attribute. The link changes how utilities become probabilities; the utilities themselves come from the comparator's fit, whose feature effects are reported in that model's own report.

ensemble.reason: There is no ensemble to be stable. This architecture is a choice *link* applied to one set of mean utilities, not a bag of independently fitted members, so seed variation here is integration noise rather than model disagreement -- and that is reported in the appendix instead.

races.reason: Representative races are chosen by how much a model's correction moved a runner's probability. This candidate applies a link to fixed mean utilities, so the movement to explain belongs to the comparator's fit and is shown in that model's report. A race chosen here would be chosen by integration noise.

topchoice.reason: Top-choice movement compares a model's first pick against the market's. This candidate is scored against its own comparator on fixed mean utilities, not against the market, so a market top-choice comparison would answer a different question than the rest of this report.

identity.comparator: the incumbent Offset model on the same margins
identity.comparator_note: The incumbent Offset, because the candidate reuses its margins exactly and changes only the link. The market anchor means a zero correction returns the market probability, so the comparison isolates the link.
identity.label: Probit Offset (market-anchored)
